dharana.rendering: When the delight of savour, the joy that comes from eating and drinking, expands, let one contemplate that state of fullness; from it comes great bliss.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: if one meditates on the full condition of the joy that comes even from satisfying bodily needs, one finds that its source is the divine pulse (spanda), and absorbed in it one experiences spiritual bliss. Singh groups verses 69–73 as examples of the senses (touch, sight, taste, sound) turned into yoga: in each, the point is the source of the joy, not the sense object. Note: the older prototype seed doors/049.json paired Door 49 with verse 49 (heart-space), which under Singh is dharana 26 (Door D-026).
dharana.technique_name: The Fullness of Savouring Food and Drink
dharana.instruction: Eat or drink slowly, savour fully, and rest attention in the fullness it brings.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position for eating or drinking, such as sitting at a table.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 72 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the joy of savouring as it spreads
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map starts small, at the taste in the mouth, and widens into a felt fullness through the whole body.
geometry.svg_hint: a small point at the mouth with soft rings widening out through a body outline
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Savour into fullness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a hurried bite slows into savouring, and the pleasure widens into a sense of fullness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn from the food to the fullness that savouring brings
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes open or closed while eating or drinking
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The expanding joy of savouring while eating or drinking
attention.secondary: The state of fullness itself, beyond the particular taste

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When the delight of savour, the joy that comes from eating and drinking, expands, let one contemplate that state of fullness; from it comes great bliss.
adiyogi.method_summary: Eat or drink something slowly. Savour it fully. As the pleasure of the taste spreads, turn attention from the food to the fullness itself, and rest in that fullness.

honesty.disclosure: Door 049 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 49 (verse 72) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.

legacy.disclosure: Vijnana Bhairava Tantra. The [retired posture]–verse pairing on this door is a School of 112 Doorways device (school_device), not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Teaching reference. Verse 49 of the Vijnana Bhairava Tantra is yukti 23 in the common enumeration. It turns attention into the space of the heart, in the inner recess of the heart-lotus, with the senses unhooked from their objects. The verse's lotus is the heart, not [retired posture], and it is not an instruction to lift [retired posture] higher. In this school the [retired posture] only serves that width. If an edition numbers the verse a line off, follow the heart-space dharana and say so.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ordinary eating only; nothing here asks for more food, fasting or any change of diet. Mind any allergies as usual. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

notes: Pregnancy: do not practice this prone backbend. A standing heart-opener, or rest, is the honest substitute.
Recent abdominal surgery, hernia, or an acute abdominal condition: do not enter the [retired posture].
Acute low-back pain, a known spondylolisthesis, or spinal instability: do not enter a backbend. Reported pain halts the machine in any case.
Neck injury, or dizziness when looking up: keep the gaze on the floor. Do not extend the cervical spine to look impressive.
Painful wrists or carpal tunnel: do not grind through the heels of the hands. Skip the [retired posture], or rest the forearms only if a teacher who can see you has already offered that variation.
Soon after a large meal: wait. A short breath and a quiet chest, face down or on the side, is enough.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 049: the fullness of savouring food and drink. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 49, verse 72.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit as you would to eat. The map starts at the taste in the mouth and widens into fullness.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Sit comfortably with something simple to eat or drink. Eyes open or closed.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Take one bite or sip slowly. Savour it. As the pleasure spreads, turn from the taste to the fullness itself. Rest there.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a hurried bite widening into fullness. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 72: when the joy of savouring food and drink expands, contemplate that fullness, and great bliss arises.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Finish the food or drink in your own time. Carry the sense of fullness into the next part of the day.
